info.title: OpenForge Companion API
info.description: Purpose-built HTTP boundary for the OpenForge Mobile Companion. Pairing request submission bootstraps trust; every existing and newly approved paired-device credential receives interactive Agent terminal access plus fixed authority for explicit Create, Start, Delete, Complete, Set Aside, Return to Board, Merge, Enqueue, Run app, and Refresh GitHub operations. Desktop-authoritative reads and mutations expose no generic command dispatch or sensitive desktop state.

post.summary: Submit a device request with a short-lived one-time pairing secret

202.description: The device is awaiting desktop approval

get.summary: Poll for the trusted desktop's pairing decision

200.description: The request was approved and the one-time credential is returned

202.description: The request is still awaiting desktop approval

Read the backend-authoritative Task Needs Attention snapshot

get.summary: List desktop Task prompt suggestions for one visible Project
get.description: Returns the effective provider, its Task prompt trigger, and the same ordered skill and command suggestions used by desktop Task Creation. This read does not execute a command or start an Implementation Run.

200.description: Current Task prompt catalog for the visible Project

post.summary: Create a backlog Task in one visible Project
post.description: Creates exactly one backlog Task using the submitted initial prompt and desktop-saved Project defaults. Clients must not automatically retry after transport uncertainty; they refresh the Project Board before offering a manual retry.

200.description: The backlog Task was created and Board resources will invalidate

get.summary: Read the approved Task detail fields

post.summary: Complete one active Task through the shared terminal lifecycle
post.description: Authenticated Task-scoped mutation. The server validates Project visibility, current doing state, and lifecycle claims; stops the Agent and Task shells; retains Completed Task reference data; and schedules safe worktree and owned-branch cleanup. Clients must not automatically retry this mutation after transport uncertainty.

200.description: Task reference data completed and cleanup accepted

post.summary: Delete one current backlog Task using terminal completion semantics
post.description: This explicit mutation is never automatically retried. The desktop verifies Task ownership, visible Project policy, current backlog state, and the per-Task lifecycle claim before preserving the Completed Task as reference data and scheduling normal runtime cleanup.

200.description: The backlog Task reached the terminal Completed Task lifecycle

post.summary: Start one backlog Task using authoritative saved defaults
post.description: Identity-only Companion Task Start. The client must not automatically retry this mutation or fail it over to another endpoint. After an uncertain transport outcome it refetches Task detail and the Project Board before offering another Start.

200.description: An Implementation Run was started and authoritative resources will invalidate

post.description: Explicit Task-scoped mutation. The client makes one attempt, then refreshes authoritative Task and Board state before offering another action.

post.description: Runs one full GitHub sync attempt. A 204 response means every scheduled phase completed without polling errors; configuration, rate-limit, and sync failures use the typed Companion error response.

204.description: Global GitHub refresh completed without errors

get.summary: Stream coarse Task and attention resource invalidations while foregrounded
get.description: Authenticated SSE stream backed by the OpenForge App Event Bus. Event data never contains internal event payloads, credentials, provider identifiers, or Agent-session identifiers. Clients refetch the named resources. Last-Event-ID resumes from the App Event Bus replay cursor when available; stream-gap requires discarding in-memory domain views and fetching fresh snapshots.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the last received SSE id field.

200.description: SSE invalidation stream. Every replayable event has an opaque id cursor.

companionDeviceBearer.description: A fixed pre-release paired-device credential authorizes desktop-authoritative reads, interactive Agent terminal attachment, and only the explicit Companion Project and Task action operations. Existing credentials inherit this authority without reapproval or migration; revocation, gateway disablement, host identity reset, credential failure, or certificate-pin failure removes access.

CompanionProtocolVersion.name: openforge-companion-protocol-version
CompanionProtocolVersion.description: Major Companion protocol version. Device authentication is evaluated before compatibility so this header never bypasses trust.
